newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

COFFEE: World market for September 4 - Robusta futures in London recovered from a four-week low of $1,550 a tonne to end firm on bargain-hunting and short-covering. Most traders expect a surplus in 1996/97, which in their view, will weigh on prices.

In New York arabica futures attempted to rebound but were not able to hold the gains and closed lower on continued speculative liquidation and some producer selling. The September/December spread remained wide and should eventually enable more coffee to come out of the woodwork to satisfy the deliveries.

Traders said there is no reason for December to maintain a strong premium after the expiration of September. September coffee ended 85 points lower at 124.20 cents/lb, while December gave up 50 points to close at 112.80 cents/lb. The back months lost between 70 and 75 points.

UNITED STATES - The United States imported 1.360 million bags of coffee in June 1996, 2 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 10.061 million bags, nearly 16 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose by 5.8 per cent to 17.105 million bags.

Major suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1996 were Guatemala (969,900 vs 854,500 bags), Mexico (2.792 vs 1.953 million bags), Colombia (1.360 vs 1.208 million bags), Thailand (574,000 vs 653,500 bags) and Vietnam (781,500 vs 435,600 bags).

The country exported 1.031 million bags of coffee in January/June 1996, nearly 30 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 fell by 22 per cent to 1.841 million bags.

ICO - Coffee exports to all destinations by exporting members to the International Coffee Organization (ICO) during July 1996 totalled 5.787 million 60-kg bags up from 5.052 million bags exported the same month the previous year, preliminary ICO estimates show.
This brought total exports in October/July 1995/96 up to 58.9 million bags which compares to 53.3 million bags the same period in 1994/95.

Brazil's market share in October/July 1995/96 dropped to 16.31 per cent from 25.29 per cent last year while Colombia's market share rose to 15.84 per cent up from 14.65 per cent in October/July 1994/95. Indonesia's exports rose sharply in October/July 1995/96 to 3.797 million bags up from 2.173 million bags the same period in 1994/95.

GUATEMALA - The president of the National Coffee Association (Anacafe) told Reuters that Guatemala will export 3.3 million 60-kg bags of coffee in 1996/97 down from 3.6 million bags exported the previous season.
According to the International Coffee Organization in London Guatemala exported 3.449 million bags in October/July 1995/96 up from 2.963 million bags exported the same period in 1994/95.
